thread:
eng-oncall-bot: [ALERT] p99 latency breach for /v1/generate (us-west-2). SLO violation detected. Current window: p95=1.2s, p99=6.3s, error-rate spike + streaming stalls. Affected pool: gpu-pool-3. Pager: @maya @alex @ron. Incident ID: INC-2026-04-06-01 :rotating_light:

maya: on it. grabbing dashboards and traces. watching p95/p99 and streaming stalls panels.

alex: joining now. I saw similar earlier today on canary but thought it was noise. what's the customer impact?

maya: preliminary — 3 customers with elevated token-latency, some streaming sessions saw 2-7s gaps between token chunks, a couple of partial responses. routing retries increased.

ron: pulling node telemetry and driver logs for gpu-pool-3. running quick health checks.

infra-bot: telemetry snapshot: gpu-pool-3 overall load normal, but node gnode-43 shows repeated GPU ECC corrected errors and thermal throttle events in the last 12m. GPU temps reported: 86-92C. power_limit_throttle_count=14. ECC_corrected=128, ECC_uncorrected=2 (recent).

maya: that matches streaming stalls — KV cache misses + driver stalls can cause long-ish tail latency. can we isolate the node?

alex: recommend cordon + drain gnode-43 and failover traffic to replicas. I'll kick routing to avoid the pool while we triage.

ron: command ready: ```kubectl cordon gnode-43 && kubectl drain gnode-43 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force```

maya: approved. cs-bot: notify affected customers (CS triage) that we're mitigating a hardware-related latency issue; we'll follow-up with impact summary.

cs-bot: Notifying: Customer A (dedicated), Customer B (hosted, high-traffic), Customer C (hosted). Short blurb sent: "We're investigating increased streaming latency impacting token pacing; mitigation underway."

alex: executing drain now. moving active sessions to gpu-pool-4 and spinning up 2 extra replicas in the fallback pool. routing rule updated: prefer gpu-pool-4 -> gpu-pool-2; fallback model variant enabled for streaming (/v1/generate) to reduce per-token work: redwood-7b-quant as temporary.

infra-bot: drain success: pods evicted from gnode-43. new routing weights applied. Quick metrics: p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 300ms within ~45s; p99 trending down from 6.3s -> 1.1s. Still watching streaming gap traces but improvement visible.

julie: nice. can we get kernel and driver logs from gnode-43 before rebooting? might need vendor ticket.

ron: grabbed dmesg + nvidia-smi output. snippets: ```[ 12:34:56 ] NVRM: Xid (PCIe) 31 ... GPU has a corrected ECC error. corrected errors++
[ 12:35:10 ] thermal daemon: GPU 0 exceeded threshold, entering power limit throttling
``` nvidia-smi --query: Temp=91C, Perf=P2, Power=280W, PowerState=18446744073709551615 (throttled).

maya: ECC_uncorrected=2 worries me. even if corrected errors were more common, intermittent uncorrected can cause driver stalls that show up as streaming stalls. safer to schedule hardware replacement. open ticket with vendor and mark node as degraded.

alex: agreed. immediate plan: 1) node drained and isolated (done). 2) boost capacity on fallback pools (done). 3) enable model fallback to reduce token-latency for active customers (done). 4) open hardware support ticket + plan replacement (ron). 5) post-incident follow-ups.

samir: putting a temporary throttling circuit-breaker in routing to detect >500ms token gaps and remove node from pool earlier in future. Also will add an alert for ECC_uncorrected > 0 in production (right now we only alert on uncorrected >5).

ron: opened vendor ticket #VT-78910 with logs and dmesg, requesting expedited GPU RMA. ETA for physical swap TBD (next-day in region if priority). ticket link: https://vendor.example.com/ticket/VT-78910

maya: severity classification: Sev2 (customers degraded, mitigation in-place, no full outage). timeline: incident started ~1891234567 (alert), mitigated routing at ~1891234590.

alex: customer impact summary for incident report: Customers A/B/C experienced increased end-to-end token latency; Customer A (dedicated) had 2 sessions with stalled streams that required reconnect; Customer B saw increased retries but no disconnects; Customer C saw token pacing slowdown. No data loss or model correctness issues observed.

julie: action items (owners):
- Replace GPU in gnode-43 and validate thermal/PCIe (ron)
- Add ECC_uncorrected single-error alert and lower threshold for corrected-error trend (samir)
- Add streaming-stall circuit-breaker in routing and a fallback to quantized model (alex)
- Update runbook for GPU thermal/ECC incidents including immediate routing steps (maya)

samir: I'll also run a cluster-wide sweep to check other nodes for rising ECC/corrected errors; early warning could prevent cascading stalls.

ron: quick note: we did a soft reboot of gnode-43 for cleaning state after drain; kernel recovered but uncorrected ECC count persists. physical RMA recommended.

maya: putting this thread into monitoring mode. if p99 remains <1.5s for next 30m we'll mark mitigated. otherwise escalate.

infra-bot: monitoring snapshot @ +5m: p95=280ms, p99=1.0s, streaming-gap alerts reduced to baseline. Hardware ticket created.

alex: nice work team. please capture timeline + evidence for postmortem. i'll prepare the draft and share in #postmortems.

cs-bot: CS notified customers with ETA for follow-up. assigned CSMs to Customer A/B/C for targeted updates.

maya: closing incident channel for the active mitigation phase. switching to follow-up thread for postmortem and action tracking. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
